FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the 
Forestry and Plantation Crops Machinery Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and 
Agriculture Division Council. 

Two men log tongs arc used for lifting, dragging and loading of small and medium size logs (normally 
up to 250 kg mass only ). 

In the formulation of this standard, assistance has been derived from Forest Operations Division, 
Forest Research Institute, Dehradun. 

The figures given in this standard arc meant only for illustrations and should not be considered as 
suggestive of any standard design. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the 
final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance 
with IS 2 : 1960 *RuIcs for rounding off numerical values ( revisedy. The number of significant places 
retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



is 13151 : 1991 



Indian Standard 



FORESTRY TOOLS — TWO MEN LOG 
TONGS — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

This standard specifies materials, dimensions and 
other requirements of two men log tongs. 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard: 



IS No, 

2102 : ( Part 1 ) 
1980 



Title 

: General tolerances for dimen- 
sions and form and position: 
Part 1 General tolerances for 
linear and angular dimensions 
( second revision ) 



12614 : 1987 Log tongs 

3 MATERIALS 

Legs of the tong shall be forged to shape and the 
composition of steel shall be: 

Carbon 0'4 to 0'6 percent 

Silicon 0'35, percent. Max 

Manganese 0*5 to 0'9 percent 

Sulphur 0*05, percent. Max 

Phosphorous 0*05, percent, Max 

Material of other components shall be mild steel. 
Wooden pole if supplied along with the tong shall 
be of good quality seasoned wood. 

3.1 Hardness 

Hardness of the legs of tong shall be 3 5 to 42 
HRC. 

4 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 

4.1 Shall be as shown in Fig. 1. 

4.2 Tolerances on dimensions shall be very coarse 
class specified in IS 2102 ( Part 1 ) : 1980. 

5 OTHER REQUIREMENTS 

The tong shall not deform and bolts shall not break 
when a load of 250 kg is applied. Wooden pole 



of 60 mm dia and 2 000 mm length is to be 
supplied alongwith the tong at the option of the 
purchaser. 

6 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

6.1 Log tongs shall be well forged to shape and 
finished smooth. They shall be free from the burrs, 
pits, sharp edges, cracks and other defects. All 
sharp corners shall be removed. 

6.2 The tongs shall open freely at joints. 

6.3 The tongs shall be coated with rust proof 
coating or grease. 

7 DESIGNATION 

Two men log tong shall be designated by its name 
and number of this Indian Standard as: 

Two Men Log Tong IS 13151 

8 MARKING AND PACKING 
8.1 Marking 

Each tong shall be marked as follows: 

a) Manufacturer's name and recpgnized trade- 
mark; 

b) Model number; 

c) Batch, code or serial numbex; and 

d) Nominal capacity. 

8.1 .1 Standard Marking 

Log tong may also ^be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 

9 PACKING 

Shall be as agreed to between the manufacturer 
and the purchaser. 

10 SAMPLING 

10.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the pur- 
chaser and supplier the sampling and criteria for 
conformity of log tong shall be done in accordance 
withthcIS 12164: 1987. 



IS 13151 : 1991 



HOLES FOR M -8 
BOLTS 




All dimensions in millimetres. 

Fig. 1 Two Men Log Tong 



Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the 
producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity 
to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of ladlan Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization* marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country.
